vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A RustSec or OSV advisory is not a weekly chore: it leaves the schedule and opens its own pull request as soon as it lands.

packageRules.description: Rust crates: keep Cargo.lock current; a major stands on its own PR so a breaking bump is never hidden in a batch.
Batch the low-risk GitHub Actions bumps into a single weekly PR (one CI run, readable queue).
Docusaurus ships its core, preset and themes on one version line; bumping them apart breaks the docs build.
The search indexer is a pair: the CLI and its default UI are published together and are only compatible at the same version.
The TLS and hashing stack backs the egress proxy's certificates and the trust gate's digests. A major here is a review, not a merge: surface it on the dashboard rather than opening a pull request.

The nixpkgs revision the bundled engines are built from. Detection only: build.rs verifies a sha256 of the resulting binaries, so a revision bump has to carry a recomputed hash and cannot be merged on its own.

customManagers.description: The pinned nixpkgs revision behind the static nix and bwrap engines, which no manager reads on its own because it lives inside a shell task.
